extracted.intended_audience: Coast Guard contracting officers, MLCPAC contract specialists, procurement analysts, and researchers studying A-76 commercial activities
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative standards used in a study of Coast Guard commercial activity contracts (A-76) including selection criteria for case studies, measures of contract performance, cost drivers, contract administration quality, and COTR responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacific Area contract selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Pacific Area contracts to observe the same contract administration as in the previously studied contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a selection criterion to ensure comparable administrative practices (so the researcher could observe the same contract administration as in the previous study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity of contract complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Similarity to the complexity of the contracts in the previous study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select contracts with comparable operational/administrative complexity so findings are comparable across cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts deleting affected billets (Subsistence Specialists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts that had deleted billets of the rate most severely affected by A-76 (Subsistence Specialists (SS)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose commercial activities that reflect the personnel impacts of A-76 (i.e., where SS billets were deleted) to study workforce consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-cost area commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial activities in high cost areas that may be difficult to support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contracts located in high-cost geographies (e.g., remote or logistics-challenged locations) to capture cost/support difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mature and current contracts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a mix of completed and ongoing contracts to observe full-life outcomes and current operational issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR role as 'eyes and ears' of Contracting Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: The COTR is supposed to be the eyes and ears of the Contracting Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the COTR acts as an effective on-site monitor and advisor to the Contracting Officer; note anti-patterns where past Housing Officer directed the COTR not to make recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR should make recommendations (avoid suppression)
rubrics_metrics.description: COTR should make recommendations to the Contracting Officer; being directed not to recommend is inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether local direction suppresses COTR reporting/recommendations; such suppression can prevent detection and management of contract conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of communication and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on letter and telephone correspondence (rather than direct observation) may cause the contract specialist to miss problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate communication practices: over-reliance on remote communication can obscure on-the-ground issues; prefer in-person/site-based feedback where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract documentation sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts should have adequate written documentation; contracts based on verbal/handshake agreements lack documentation and create administrative problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contract files for completeness; lack of documentation hinders effective administration and requires specialists to 'patch-up' contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity/unambiguity of specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications must be clear and unambiguous; ambiguous specifications can be exploited by contractors to negotiate additional payment for work that should be within scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Statements of Work / Performance Work Statements for ambiguity; ambiguous scope has historically led to negotiated higher prices for 'additional' work such as exercise meals.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR training and debriefing
rubrics_metrics.description: COTRs should receive training and debriefing; lack of prior COTR experience necessitates MLCPAC-provided training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether assigned COTRs have training and whether incoming COTRs are debriefed by predecessors; training history correlated with COTR confidence and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of deductions for unsatisfactory performance as performance metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Deductions taken for unsatisfactory performance (or lack thereof) used as an indicator of contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check contract payment/deduction records; note that small deductions (e.g., $446 for 14 minor discrepancies) may not always be consistently recorded in contract files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking cost increases via contract line items
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing costs (e.g., housing maintenance) as separate line items may be necessary to track cost increases and measure cost-effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate contract structure: separate line items facilitate monitoring of cost trends and effectiveness; consolidated line items may make tracking difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying sources of cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize primary sources of cost increases (DOL wage determinations, negotiated extensions, economic price adjustments, added work such as exercise meals, and special events like Desert Storm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing cost changes, disaggregate by source and incorporate wage determinations and negotiated settlements; monitor incorporation of new DOL determinations that can nearly double costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of modifications and deobligations to measure actual costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract modifications and year-end deobligations indicate differences between estimated/obligated funds and actual performance costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track mods and deobligations carefully; deobligations occur when actual costs are below estimates (e.g., fewer meals sold), and can offset wage-driven cost increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of contractor management and key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Retention of experienced contractor personnel (e.g., project managers) contributes to successful performance and smooth transitions between contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate contractor staffing continuity (PM stability, experienced supervisors) as a qualitative performance factor; the presence of an experienced PM was cited as a major reason for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor financial stability and contingency risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess contractor financial condition and contingency plans; contractor bankruptcy or instability poses risk and may limit Government's ability to replace contractor performance (insufficient government SSs available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contractor financial health in risk assessments; consider availability of government personnel to assume service if contractor defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost reduction feasibility tied to requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs in some contracts can only be decreased by reducing requirements (e.g., reducing number of personnel or meal requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering cost control measures, examine whether requirements can be altered; otherwise cost drivers like wages may be unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and procurement outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Small business competitions and competitive bidding can drive down contract costs; non-responsible bidders may change award outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether procurement method (8(a), negotiated award, small business competition) produced cost savings and whether responsible bidder determinations affected final price.
